headline: AI dip-buyers return even as Nvidia's own story darkens
body: Wall Street has been trading in sharp swings this week rather than settling into a clean trend. A hotter-than-expected October CPI print pushed the 10-year Treasury yield back toward 5% and revived talk of the Fed holding rates or even hiking in December instead of cutting again, with at least one Fed official signaling openness to a swift, larger response if inflation keeps running hot. Stocks sold off on that news, then rebounded hard the next session as the AI trade reasserted itself, led by a strong earnings beat from a major AI-infrastructure name that pushed the Nasdaq toward one of its best weeks in months. The whiplash pattern suggests dip-buying reflexes are intact, but the speed of the round-trip also points to a market that reprices quickly on single data points and headlines rather than moving with settled conviction either way.

Beneath the index-level rebound, the tape is less unified than the headlines suggest. Nvidia itself diverged from the broader AI rally, falling sharply after hours on fresh reports about its CEO's personal conduct and renewed questions about his standing at the company — a company-specific headline risk now running alongside, and at times against, the sector's valuation debate. Capital rotating into other AI-infrastructure and chip names even as the bellwether stumbles reads as a market compartmentalizing single-stock risk rather than letting it spread into a broader AI selloff. Retail-sentiment trackers didn't turn up a clear, current read today, so this take leans more on price action and headline flow than on social-media positioning — a sign of thin signal there, not of calm.
